headline: Revenue grows on PMG deal; margins and profit stay pressured
summary_short: Revenue rose to $8,512.7M (+8.3% q/q, +6.0% y/y) on the PMG commercial-truck acquisition and same-store gains, but net income fell 2.3% y/y to $260.4M as new-vehicle gross margin compressed and PMG's earnings became newly taxable.
summary_long: Revenue grew on the PMG acquisition plus same-store new (+5.0%) and used (+9.9%) vehicle revenue; new-vehicle gross profit per unit fell 11.8% same-store on competitive selling conditions and fading tariff-related pull-forward. Service & parts gross profit grew 3.4% same-store on higher labor rates and a favorable U.K. mix shift. Commercial truck demand stayed soft (new units -7.8% same-store) on weak Class 8 freight, though used-truck sales rebounded sharply. Net income fell as PMG's earnings, untaxed pre-acquisition, became subject to corporate tax, lifting the effective tax rate to 26.8% from 25.3%. Long-term debt rose $713.3M y/y funding the deal; cash fell to $69.5M. Board declared a $1.44/share Q3 dividend, up from $1.42.

Penske completed a common-control acquisition of Penske Motor Group (PMG) on November 19, 2025; per the filing, all historical comparative periods have been retrospectively recast to include PMG as if always consolidated, so y/y and q/q comparisons already reflect PMG in both periods. That recast also means PMG's income, previously untaxed as a pass-through partnership, is only taxable in the consolidated group from the acquisition date forward, which by itself explains part of the y/y net-income and EPS decline despite higher pretax income. Six-months 2026 results include a $90.9M pretax gain ($67.5M after-tax, $1.03/share) from the sale of U.S. retail automotive franchises, versus a $52.3M pretax gain ($38.9M after-tax, $0.58/share) in the prior-year six months — both one-offs embedded in the reported net income figures. drivers.explanation: Grew on the PMG acquisition base plus same-store gains: new-vehicle revenue +5.0% same-store, used-vehicle +9.9% same-store, service & parts +2.0% same-store.

New-vehicle same-store gross profit per unit fell 11.8% on a competitive selling environment and fading prior-year tariff-related sales pull-forward, offsetting used-vehicle and service & parts gross-profit gains.
Retail commercial truck new-unit sales fell 7.8% same-store on a weak Class 8 freight environment, compressing truck segment gross profit even as used-truck demand rebounded.
PMG's earnings, untaxed as a pass-through prior to the November 2025 acquisition, became subject to corporate income tax in the consolidated group, lifting the effective tax rate to 26.8% from 25.3%.
Debt rose to fund the PMG acquisition and related net borrowings; cash fell as it was directed toward the deal, dividends, and buybacks.

Six-months 2026 net income includes a $90.9M gain ($1.03/share after-tax) from selling U.S. retail auto franchises, versus a smaller $52.3M gain a year earlier — both one-off, not core operating performance.
